beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new, just a title

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: sharing the agent itself is the wrong frame; you share context, a skill, output or an interface

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: nothing new, homework I didn't do

beats.trigger: **Name** the likely adoption failure before it happens, including the social failure that's hardest to see
beats.got: nothing new, a list of verbs

beats.trigger: who's the one person who came to mind just now?
beats.got: I thought of our sales lead right away, and I haven't asked her anything

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: start from their job, not my tool. fair, but I've heard JTBD before

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: the agent interviews me about my teammate and the test is whether the answer is specific. I'd have skipped the read step

beats.trigger: *"Share the whole agent"* is a vendor pitch and is NOT on the list.
beats.got: four sharing shapes. I always just handed people the repo, so this is a useful list

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new, a handoff screen

beats.trigger: find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it
beats.got: nothing new, setup for the next two steps

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: look for the one obstacle that sits under the others, not the first technical limit I'd see. my instinct is always the technical one

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: my plans would be exactly that: tech file done, people file full of UNASSIGNED. I haven't checked who maintains the sales setup

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans, imagines the failure
beats.got: nothing new, a handoff screen

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: nothing new, the plans are guesses until tested

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: flip the adoption question into what has to be true for them to switch. that's a better question than the ones I ask

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: a premortem where the sales team quietly went back to their spreadsheet. that felt too plausible. I'd build bigger instead of talking to someone

beats.trigger: Test the switch, not the solution.
beats.got: a recap of the exercise

beats.trigger: The rest of this is about the person on the other end of your plan.
beats.got: nothing new, a transition

beats.trigger: A good interview finds a third outcome past speed and quality: a dependency removed, an anxiety gone, a scope widened.
beats.got: mostly a repeat. the third outcome idea is a bit new

beats.trigger: Hand someone the agent file and they run it, get a generic answer, and quietly stop.
beats.got: the agent file is only instructions; the real work is in the memory and corrections. I've seen this happen after I shared my setups, and nobody told me they stopped

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all, which is why the product being sold as a shared agent is always three of the four parts, with the fourth still sitting with whoever built it.
beats.got: context, boundary and checks copy but accountability doesn't. so I'm the owner of anything I ship, which I hadn't thought about

beats.trigger: The interface is the first piece whose shape depends on somebody whose calendar you do not control.
beats.got: nothing new, a short bridge

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: a real story where agents did the analysis and the decision still died because leadership hadn't done it themselves. no hype in it, and it's the first thing that made me doubt my plan

beats.trigger: Access is a switch somebody flips, and it completes in a minute.
beats.got: access and adoption are different numbers. true, I already knew it

beats.trigger: we know more than we can tell.
beats.got: people only take up what resembles their own work. a bit abstract

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: my agent competes with the spreadsheet or the gut call. the sales team has one, and I never looked at it

beats.trigger: Whether they pick it up is their decision, made for their own reasons, on a Tuesday you will not be in the room for.
beats.got: I can't force adoption. a bit preachy

beats.trigger: The technical plan fills quickly. The people plan stalls on names.
beats.got: missing names are the real finding. that's me with the sales setup, and nobody there asked for it

beats.trigger: The agent reviews, rewrites the sharing artifact in place, and reports what changed.
beats.got: nothing new, an agent reviews its own file. I'd skip it

beats.trigger: Save the conversation. It's the bridge to when work resumes.
beats.got: nothing new, process housekeeping

beats.trigger: Access is easy; absorption is scarce.
beats.got: nothing new, a summary

beats.trigger: Come to Module 8 without one tested assumption or named person and you'll be reconstructing the contact while the opening exercise is already using the evidence.
beats.got: I need to talk to one real person before next module, and that's the homework I'd avoid

beats.trigger: The sharing plan leaves the room and meets the organisation.
beats.got: nothing new, a teaser

take_homes: you can't hand over an agent. context, skill, output or interface travel, but accountability stays with whoever built it, and that is me
my sales team setup is a guess until I ask one person how they do the job today. I hadn't checked who would maintain it
the question to ask is what would have to be true for them to drop the spreadsheet and switch, not how I get them to adopt this

monday.move: ask our sales lead how she does her weekly pipeline prep now, and put one name on the maintainer line before I build more
monday.stop_condition: if she says she doesn't need it, or nobody will own it, I stop building the org-wide version
monday.blocker: I'll want to keep building instead of asking, and nobody outside engineering asked for this

misconception.why: the module never went after 'checking is for beginners' directly, and I'd still skip review steps on my own agent output. but accountability not copying, plus the leadership story, made me see that good output still doesn't mean anyone will use it or answer for it. that is about adoption, not whether the output is right, so only partly shaken.

one_line: the exercises are slower than I like and I'd skip half of them, but the three-parts-copy bit and the leadership story were things I hadn't heard, and they made me doubt my sales-team plan.
